section.title: Paying for it
section.intro: The most expensive part about college in Ireland isn't the tuition fees, it's the living costs. When combined, it can be expensive, and hard work to keep on top of. Thankfully there are some options which can help keep you focused on your studies.

items.body:
HEAR offers college places on reduced points and extra support once you're in, to school leavers from disadvantaged backgrounds. It's ran by universities through the CAO.

It's assessed on your household, so you need to apply and show your circumstances.

blocks.heading: What you actually get
blocks.text: A place on lower points than the published requirement, and support once you're there, such as study help, and in some cases money. It's the same course, exams degree as everyone else.

blocks.heading: Check the deadline early
blocks.text: HEAR goes in with your CAO application, but its closing date is well before the main CAO one. Supporting documents are due even earlier. You are much better off looking for the deadlines at the start of 6th year rather than after the mocks

blocks.heading: Paperwork
blocks.text: Proof of income and evidence of your circumstances. Start early and ask your guidance counsellor to help

blocks.heading: Applying costs you nothing
blocks.text: If you're not eligible, your normal CAO application is used

items.summary: A way into college on reduced points if your circumstances qualify.

myths.reality: It covers far more than you think, so it is better to apply and see what happens rather than not doing anything.

myths.myth: People will know I got in on reduced points.
myths.reality: It isn't on your degree and nobody in your lectures is told.

items.body:
SUSI is the national student grant. Depending on your household income and circumstances, it can cover your student contribution and also pay you a maintenance grant to live on.

Applying is free, with the threshold higher than most people expect, so it's always better to try apply

blocks.heading: Two separate things
blocks.text: One part covers your fees and the other pays you money to live on. They're assessed separately, so you might get one and not the other, and the maintenance grant is higher if college is far from home.

blocks.heading: Apply early
blocks.text: You don't need an offer to apply. If you wait until August, you might be waiting until September for the money.

blocks.heading: College-backed emergency fund
blocks.text: Most colleges run a Student Assistance Fund for students hit by costs they didn't see coming. It's discretionary and confidential.

items.summary: Covers fees and sometimes even maintenance grants

myths.reality: The limits are higher than people think, and they change every year. Check the current ones on susi.ie.
There's also a maintenance grant. Paid directly to you, it can help fund your cost of living whilst studying.
